Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Moderators started asking for this:

> As a moderator, I want to reuse my quiz at another conference, or share it with a colleague who runs Quizzy too.

The quiz page gets the "Export" link. It opens a page that shows the quiz as JSON inside a `<pre>` element (the only `<pre>` on the page), ready to copy.

`/moderate` gets the "Import quiz" button. It opens a page with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. Importing always creates a new quiz, even if a quiz with the same title exists, and opens its page.

The format:

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `questions` and `options` keep their order.
- On import, `active` is optional (`true` by default), and `correct` is optional (`false` by default).
- The export always writes both, and it writes exactly these keys: the quiz title and its questions, nothing else. The export is only for moving quiz contents.
- Imported questions follow the same rules as the question form.

When the JSON is invalid or breaks a rule, the page shows an error and nothing is imported: not the quiz, not a part of its questions.

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (stored under `storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, and Stimulus. All CSS, JS, and the `Inter-latin.woff2` webfont are served locally with no external network dependencies.

## Data Model

- `quizzes`: `title` (string, required, whitespace trimmed). `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `questions`: `quiz_id` (FK), `body` (text, required), `position` (integer, required), `active` (boolean, default `true`). `has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `options`: `question_id` (FK), `body` (string, required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer, required).

Future live-quiz releases can build `runs` / `participants` / `answers` referencing `quizzes`, `questions`, and `options` directly; option updates preserve existing `option.id` values when edited in place.

## Moderator Area & Auth

- All moderator routes are namespaced under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, which enforces HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Missing or wrong credentials return `401 Unauthorized`.
- `GET /up` (health check) and `GET /` (landing page) do not require moderator authentication.

## Frontend & Browser Compatibility Insights

- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` are imported from `docs/mockups/`, with small app-specific additions in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css`.
- `app/javascript/application.js` loads Stimulus controllers without auto-starting Turbo Drive so browsers authenticating via URL-embedded Basic Auth (`http://user:pass@host/moderate`) do not hit Chromium's `History.replaceState` `SecurityError`.

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }

  normalizes :body, with: ->(value) { value.strip }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true

  before_validation :assign_position, on: :create

  def save_with_option_rows(rows)
    cleaned = Array(rows).map do |row|
      {
        id: row[:id].presence&.to_i,
        body: row[:body].to_s.strip,
        correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(row[:correct]) || false
      }
    end

    non_empty = cleaned.reject { |r| r[:body].empty? }

    valid?
    errors.add(:base, "Add at least two options") if non_empty.size < 2
    errors.add(:base, "Mark at least one option as correct") if non_empty.none? { |r| r[:correct] }

    return false if errors.any?

    transaction do
      save!

      existing_by_id = options.index_by(&:id)
      kept_ids = []

      non_empty.each_with_index do |row, index|
        pos = index + 1
        if row[:id] && existing_by_id.key?(row[:id])
          option = existing_by_id[row[:id]]
          option.update!(body: row[:body], correct: row[:correct], position: pos)
          kept_ids << option.id
        else
          option = options.create!(body: row[:body], correct: row[:correct], position: pos)
          kept_ids << option.id
        end
      end

      options.where.not(id: kept_ids).destroy_all
    end

    true
  end

  def move_up!
    move_by!(-1)
  end

  def move_down!
    move_by!(1)
  end

  def assign_position
    return if position.present? || quiz.nil?

    self.position = (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
  end

  def move_by!(delta)
    transaction do
      ordered = quiz.questions.ordered.to_a
      index = ordered.index { |q| q.id == id }

            total_count: @quiz.questions.count

      when Array

        body_val = row.key?("body") ? row["body"] : row[:body]
        correct_val = row.key?("correct") ? row["correct"] : row[:correct]

        {
          id: id_val.presence,
          body: body_val.to_s,
          correct: ActiveModel::Type::Boolean.new.cast(correct_val) || false

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/quiz/importer.rb
class Quiz::Importer
  include ActiveModel::Model

  attr_accessor :json
  attr_reader :quiz

  def import
    errors.clear
    @quiz = nil

    raw = json.to_s
    if raw.strip.empty?
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON can't be blank")
      return false
    end

    data = parse_json(raw)
    return false if errors.any?

    normalized = validate_and_normalize(data)
    return false if errors.any?

    ActiveRecord::Base.transaction do
      created_quiz = Quiz.create!(title: normalized[:title])

      normalized[:questions].each_with_index do |q_attrs, q_idx|
        question = created_quiz.questions.create!(
          body: q_attrs[:text],
          active: q_attrs[:active],
          position: q_idx + 1
        )

        q_attrs[:options].each_with_index do |o_attrs, o_idx|
          question.options.create!(
            body: o_attrs[:text],
            correct: o_attrs[:correct],
            position: o_idx + 1
          )
        end
      end

      @quiz = created_quiz
    end

    true
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => e
    errors.add(:base, e.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence)
    @quiz = nil
    false
  end

  private

  def parse_json(raw)
    JSON.parse(raw)
  rescue JSON::JSONError => e
    errors.add(:base, "Invalid JSON: #{e.message}")
    nil
  end

  def validate_and_normalize(data)
    unless data.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "Quiz JSON must be a JSON object")
      return nil
    end

    title = validate_title(data)
    questions = validate_questions(data)

    return nil if errors.any?

    { title: title, questions: questions }
  end

  def validate_title(data)
    unless data.key?("title")
      errors.add(:base, "Title can't be blank")
      return nil
    end

    title = data["title"]
    unless title.is_a?(String)
      errors.add(:base, "Title must be a string")
      return nil
    end

    stripped = title.strip
    if stripped.blank?
      errors.add(:base, "Title can't be blank")
      return nil
    end

    stripped
  end

  def validate_questions(data)
    unless data.key?("questions") && data["questions"].is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "Questions must be an array")
      return []
    end

    data["questions"].each_with_index.map do |raw_question, index|
      validate_question(raw_question, index + 1)
    end
  end

  def validate_question(raw_question, number)
    unless raw_question.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{number} must be an object")
      return nil
    end

    text = validate_question_text(raw_question, number)
    active = validate_boolean(raw_question, "active", default: true, label: "Question #{number}: active")
    options = validate_options(raw_question, number)

    { text: text, active: active, options: options }
  end

  def validate_question_text(raw_question, number)
    unless raw_question.key?("text")
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{number}: text can't be blank")
      return nil
    end

    text = raw_question["text"]
    unless text.is_a?(String)
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{number}: text must be a string")
      return nil
    end

    stripped = text.strip
    if stripped.blank?
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{number}: text can't be blank")
      return nil
    end

    stripped
  end

  def validate_options(raw_question, number)
    unless raw_question.key?("options") && raw_question["options"].is_a?(Array)
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{number}: options must be an array")
      return []
    end

    raw_options = raw_question["options"]
    error_count_before = errors.size

    options = raw_options.each_with_index.map do |raw_option, opt_index|
      validate_option(raw_option, number, opt_index + 1)
    end

    option_errors_added = errors.size > error_count_before

    if raw_options.size < 2
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{number}: add at least two options")
    end

    if !option_errors_added && options.compact.none? { |opt| opt[:correct] }
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{number}: mark at least one option as correct")
    end

    options
  end

  def validate_option(raw_option, question_number, option_number)
    unless raw_option.is_a?(Hash)
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{question_number}, option #{option_number} must be an object")
      return nil
    end

    stripped = nil
    if !raw_option.key?("text")
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{question_number}, option #{option_number}: text can't be blank")
    elsif !raw_option["text"].is_a?(String)
      errors.add(:base, "Question #{question_number}, option #{option_number}: text must be a string")
    else
      stripped = raw_option["text"].strip
      if stripped.blank?
        errors.add(:base, "Question #{question_number}, option #{option_number}: text can't be blank")
      end
    end

    correct = validate_boolean(
      raw_option,
      "correct",
      default: false,
      label: "Question #{question_number}, option #{option_number}: correct"
    )

    { text: stripped, correct: correct }
  end

  def validate_boolean(hash, key, default:, label:)
    return default unless hash.key?(key)

    value = hash[key]
    return value if value == true || value == false

    errors.add(:base, "#{label} must be true or false")
    default
  end
end
EOF

# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (stored under `storage/`), Propshaft, Importmap, and Stimulus. All CSS, JS, and the `Inter-latin.woff2` webfont are served locally with no external network dependencies.

## Data Model

- `quizzes`: `title` (string, required, whitespace trimmed). `has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `questions`: `quiz_id` (FK), `body` (text, required), `position` (integer, required), `active` (boolean, default `true`). `has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy`.
- `options`: `question_id` (FK), `body` (string, required), `correct` (boolean, default `false`), `position` (integer, required).

Future live-quiz releases can build `runs` / `participants` / `answers` referencing `quizzes`, `questions`, and `options` directly; option updates preserve existing `option.id` values when edited in place.

## Quiz Export & Import

- `Quiz::Exporter` (`app/models/quiz/exporter.rb`) serializes a quiz to pretty-printed JSON with strictly the content keys: `title`, `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options` with `text`, `correct`), always writing both `active` and `correct` and preserving `position` order. Future runtime data (runs, participants, answers, scores) must never be added to this export payload.
- `Moderate::ExportsController#show` (`GET /moderate/quizzes/:quiz_id/export`) renders the exported JSON inside the page's sole `<pre>` element (`code-block`), with a Stimulus `copy_code_controller.js` button that works over both HTTPS and plain HTTP.
- `Quiz::Importer` (`app/models/quiz/importer.rb`) is an `ActiveModel::Model` that validates JSON syntax, structure, types, and all quiz/question rules before creating a new `Quiz` (and its ordered `Question`/`Option` rows) inside a single database transaction. On import, `active` defaults to `true` and `correct` defaults to `false`; importing always creates a new quiz even if one with the same title exists; any error rolls back/aborts cleanly so nothing is created.
- `Moderate::ImportsController` (`GET /moderate/import`, `POST /moderate/import`) renders the `"Quiz JSON"` form and redirects to the newly created quiz page on success, or re-renders with `422 Unprocessable Entity` and preserved input on error.

## Moderator Area & Auth

- All moderator routes are namespaced under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`, which enforces HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Missing or wrong credentials return `401 Unauthorized`.
- `GET /up` (health check) and `GET /` (landing page) do not require moderator authentication.

## Frontend & Browser Compatibility Insights

- `app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css` and `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2` are imported from `docs/mockups/`, with small app-specific additions in `app/assets/stylesheets/application.css`.
- `app/javascript/application.js` loads Stimulus controllers without auto-starting Turbo Drive so browsers authenticating via URL-embedded Basic Auth (`http://user:pass@host/moderate`) do not hit Chromium's `History.replaceState` `SecurityError`.
- `question_active_controller.js` resolves PATCH URLs against `window.location.origin` (not `document.baseURI`) so `fetch()` works reliably under both `Authorization` header auth and URL-embedded Basic Auth, with queued requests and `keepalive: true`.
- `option_rows_controller.js` dynamically adds/removes option rows and renumbers labels (`Option N`, `Option N is correct`) cleanly.
- `preview_controller.js` runs preview entirely in memory (no DB/session/storage writes), stepping through active questions in order and resetting cleanly on "Start over" or reload.

## Running in Production

`bin/serve` sets `RAILS_ENV=production` (default), runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes Puma bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`, `hosts.clear`, `public_file_server.enabled = true`).
